raw_response:
I am 74 years old and I have worked these fields in Quzhou for 54 years. I only went to primary school. Everything I know I learned from my father and from doing it with my own hands. My two sons work in Handan city, so it is just me and my old wife on the 5 mu now.

I plant 4 mu in wheat-maize rotation, and 1 mu in cotton. I never start from a blank slate. I do what I did last year, and if I change anything, it is because I saw Lao Zhang or Old Wang get a better result first.

For winter wheat on the 4 mu: I sow in October using the improved Jimai variety, about 25 jin per mu. I spread one 100-jin bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base. Then at green-up I topdress 20 jin of urea per mu, and at jointing another 30 jin. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times — winter, jointing, and grain filling. I spray twice for weeds and bugs. I rotary till before sowing. I expect 500 kg per mu. Last year I got 480, so this is reasonable.

For summer maize on those same 4 mu: After wheat harvest in June, I hire the rotary tiller to come through fast, then I sow hybrid Zhengdan 958, about 5 jin per mu. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and at big trumpet stage I spread 50 jin of urea per mu. That is about 20 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice. I spray twice. Expected yield is 600 kg per mu.

For cotton on 1 mu: I plant my saved traditional cotton seed in late April. Cotton takes a lot of work, but I have done it my whole life. I plough the field deep in spring. I put down 60 jin of compound fertilizer and 20 jin of potassium fertilizer per mu — cotton needs more potassium. That is about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 12 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times and spray five times for bollworm and aphids. Picking is hard on my back now, but I expect 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive now, but I would rather put on a little too much than risk a bad harvest. If the harvest fails, I have nothing. If I waste some fertilizer, I only lose the money for that bag. When I am unsure, I do what I did before. Change is risky. I watch my neighbors. If everyone around me applies a certain amount, I do something similar. That is how I have farmed for 54 years.
